entries.note: DOI -> PMID 27752710 (Diabetologia; online 17 Oct 2016, issue 2017). Quote verbatim in PMC full text (PubMed strips the sub/superscripts). No patient NHE1 read-out exists, so untested holds. Year would be 2016 if the atlas uses first-online dates.

Status and year stand; model field does not. FDA S-020 pharm/tox review (draft said unfetchable; it downloads, 11 MB) names the sponsor's HF nonclinical package: ob/ob mice 1.5 and 4.0 mg/kg/day, BTBR ob/ob 1 mg/kg/day; clinical dose carried over from T2D (5 or 10 mg/day).

Byrne DOI/quote verified (PMC full text); untested holds, no model-vs-patient comparison anywhere, FDA review only summarises model data. But the class's FDA-filed model is the T2D mouse, whose cardiac use starts pre-EMPA-REG (Lin 2014 db/db). Start cell 2014; keep Byrne 2017.

missing: efficacy 2014 untested, model 'Type 2 diabetic mouse (db/db)': Lin 2014, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12933-014-0148-1 (online 26 Oct 2014, 11 months before EMPA-REG). Empagliflozin 'significantly ameliorated cardiac interstitial fibrosis, pericoronary arterial fibrosis, coronary arterial thickening, cardiac macrophage infiltration' in db/db mice. This is the same model class the sponsor later filed with FDA for the HFrEF indication (ob/ob, BTBR ob/ob), so under the brief's 'relied on' rule the efficacy strip starts here, not 2017. It is a glucose-lowering finding in a diabetic heart, not a prediction of an HF-outcome benefit; the draft's judgement already says so correctly, but the context note's 'every model here was built to explain a clinical result' is then only true of the non-diabetic HF models.

Older phlorizin precedents, same caveat (diabetic hearts, glycaemia-driven, no HF prediction): Hong 2007, https://doi.org/10.1152/ajpendo.00256.2007 ('cardiac remodeling with ventricular hypertrophy that was ameliorated following chronic phloridzin treatment in Ins2(Akita) mice'); Cai 2013, https://doi.org/10.1155/2013/263845 (phlorizin protective in db/db diabetic cardiomyopathy). Full pre-Sept-2015 PubMed sweep (36 records, 2000-2015) found nothing that predicted a heart-failure benefit; the only other cardiac signals are a phloridzin SERCA2a inhibition (Olson 2005, https://doi.org/10.1124/jpet.105.092940) and the Hamouda 2014 negative inotropy the draft already cites. The draft's central chronology claim survives for HF models.

FDA review, NDA 202293 S-020 (Farxiga HFrEF, approved 5 May 2020; pharm/tox review signed 7 Apr 2020), https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/202293Orig1s020.pdf. Draft marks it unverified (bot block); curl with a browser UA retrieves it. Quotes to carry: 'the sponsor submitted nonclinical proof of concept studies in mouse models of type 2 diabetes'; 'Study results were consistent with a dapagliflozin-induced improvement in cardiac structure and function in diabetic animals. These studies did not address cardiac effects in healthy animals.'; 'This drug is approvable from a nonclinical perspective based on data provided in the original application and FDA reviews for treatment of diabetes.'; summary review: 'The Applicant did not conduct additional clinical pharmacology studies to support the proposed indication. There were no relevant nonclinical data for review.' The three filed studies are Nonclinical HF 001 (ob/ob, dapagliflozin 1.5/4.0 mg/kg/day drinking water), HF 002 (BTBR ob/ob, 1 mg/kg/day, 8 weeks = Ye 2017, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10557-017-6725-2, Apr 2017), HF 003 (BTBR ob/ob cardiofibroblasts in vitro).

safety cell is empty; consider one untested entry. The S-020 review states 'No additional nonclinical studies were conducted to support the proposed indication' and rests HF safety on the T2D toxicology package, whose silence DAPA-HF then tested ('The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups'). The ad-amyloid example carries a general-tox safety model, so house style allows it. No primary source makes the model-vs-patient comparison, so it stays untested.

Wording: 'First HF model for the class' overstates Byrne. Earlier post-EMPA-REG, pre-Byrne cardiac models: Lee 2017, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2017.01.035 (Jan 2017, non-diabetic infarcted rat hearts, fibrosis); Shi 2017, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11010-017-3018-9 (Apr 2017, zebrafish HF biomarkers, titled 'clues to the EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial?'); Ye 2017 (Apr 2017, BTBR ob/ob cardiac function). Byrne is the first non-diabetic mouse with established reduced-EF HF; say that. All are 2017, so no year change.
rule_questions: 'Best model' when the sponsor filed model X but the regulator says it did not rely on it: the FDA pharm/tox review names T2D mouse models as the sponsor's HF package, then approves 'based on data ... for treatment of diabetes', and the summary review says 'no relevant nonclinical data'. Is the atlas model the sponsor's filed model (T2D mouse, strip starts 2014), the regulator's relied-on model (none), or the first disease-matched published model (Byrne, 2017)? This decides the efficacy start year and whether the context note's chronology claim stands as written.

First-online vs issue year for untested entries: Baartscheer is online Oct 2016 / issue 2017; EMPA-TROPISM results online Nov 2020 / issue Jan 2021. The brief says 'year the comparison was published' without choosing.

Engagement model: the draft tracks the post-hoc cardiac NHE1 proposal; the class's own target is renal SGLT2 (glucosuria), which the HF-model animals (Byrne: urine glucose rose; sponsor's ob/ob: 'increased urinary glucose excretion') and, reportedly, HF patients both show. No published model-vs-patient comparison was found for either, so untested holds, but the model label and start year differ. Not checked: patient glucosuria/natriuresis studies in HF (e.g. Boorsma 2021 EJHF) were outside budget.

EMPA-TROPISM: a design paper (2019) states the pig-model-derived hypothesis and the result paper (2021) confirms it, but no single primary source makes the comparison (result abstract silent; full text paywalled). Does a design-plus-result pair count as 'a published comparison' for `same`? The draft withheld it; I agree under a strict reading, but the rule does not decide it.
Safety cell: empty list vs an untested entry for the inherited T2D toxicology package when the FDA review explicitly says no HF-specific nonclinical safety work was done.
